subject: SKU metering, packaging options, and partner margin scenarios
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Milton <sara.milton@acmeanalytics.com>, Mark Chu <mark.chu@resellercorp.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 29 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SKU metering options and partner margin scenarios for Acme private offer

Hi Sara / Mark —

Thanks for taking the time to explore a private offer for Acme. Before we lock in a PO template, we want to confirm a few packaging and channel margin points so the marketplace listing and reseller passback reconcile with Acme's billing expectations. I attached a first pass (pricing-model-v3.xlsx) and a quick sku-mapping-draft.csv.

Key questions:
- Metering unit: For Azure marketplace we can map to vCPU-month or a higher-level seat/usage metric (API call/tokens). Which aligns best with Acme's internal billing? (Sara, do you have preference for unit-of-measure so we avoid double-billing?)
- Tiering / discounts: We can implement commit-based tiers in the private offer (example: list price, then 10% / 20% discounts by commit bucket). Do you prefer a single blended discount or discrete bucketed discounts that appear on the invoice?
- Channel margin and passback: Mark — what reseller margin will you need at each commit tier to make the economics work for your sales motion? We want the private offer to reflect net revenue splits clearly so downstream invoicing and revenue recognition are clean.
- Minimums / floor: Do we need a minimum consumption floor for the channel passback to trigger? For example, if usage < $X in a month, passback is prorated.

Proposed next step: if you can share a simple target margin table (Row: Tier, Columns: Acme list price, discount, reseller margin %), we’ll translate to private offer SKUs and produce example net revenue waterfalls.

Attachments referenced: pricing-model-v3.xlsx (workbook with sample waterfalls), sku-mapping-draft.csv (example meter mapping). I’ll loop Karhtik and Ben for margin ops and distributor implications.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m call if helpful.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0191
Attachments: pricing-model-v3.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB), sku-mapping-draft.csv (csv, 14KB)

Subject: Re: SKU metering options and partner margin scenarios for Acme private offer

Tessa / Sara —

Quick read-through — thanks for the draft. A couple of points from ResellerCorp's side:
- Margin appetite: For an initial private offer, we’d be comfortable with 18% margin on the base tier (0–$250k ARR), and 12% margin on overage/expansion. We can increase to 22% if Acme commits to a multi-year guarantee.
- Prefer discrete buckets on the invoice (easier for our finance reconciliations).
- Passback trigger: we need a monthly floor (suggest $5k/month) below which the passback is zero; otherwise we end up with lots of administrative micro-payments.

If you can provide the waterfall example with these numbers plugged in, we’ll confirm internally. Also — we’ll need a reseller addendum signature (DocuSign) to formalize commission flow; can you attach your standard reseller term-sheet?

Mark
Mark Chu
VP Channels, ResellerCorp
mark.chu@resellercorp.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SKU metering options and partner margin scenarios for Acme private offer

Tessa / team —

Thanks for the draft and for looping us in. A few internal notes on feasibility and accounting:

1) Azure meter mapping: vCPU-month is the cleanest for infrastructure-like usage. It maps nicely to our runtime billing and avoids token->dollar estimation disagreements. If Acme wants token-based, we should add a conversion clause in the private offer (e.g., 1M tokens = X vCPU-hours) and include the conversion table in the Doc.

2) Discounting structure options (recommended):
   - Option A (simple): Single blended discount applied to list price based on annual commit (e.g., 15% blended at $250k+). Easier for marketplace UI but less granular for channel margin.
   - Option B (bucketed): 2-3 discrete buckets visible on invoice (0-$150k: list, $150k-$500k: 10% off, $500k+: 20% off). Better for partner commissions because we can calculate margin by bucket.

3) Channel margin waterfall (example):
   - List price -> private-offer discount -> gross revenue
   - Apply reseller commission % on gross or net? Recommend on gross (pre-discount) only if reseller has to take credit risk; otherwise apply on net-revenue after discount. ResellerCorp’s ask (18% base) would be on net revenue in most of our standard deals.

4) Minimums/floor: Agree with a $5k monthly floor to reduce churn and administrative overhead; passback pro-rated if monthly usage > floor.

5) Accounting & rev rec: Ben, we’ll need a small worksheet that shows how the passback will appear in our net revenue lines and whether any contra-revenue entries are required for marketplace settlements. I attached a stub in pricing-model-v3.xlsx but will expand if this direction is chosen.

If we go with Option B (bucketed) + reseller margin on net, we can model 3 scenarios and present to Acme next week. Tessa — want me to produce the 3-scenario table?

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Marketplace Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SKU metering options and partner margin scenarios for Acme private offer

Sara / Mark —

Thanks for the quick responses — consolidating next steps and a concrete example below. I've attached an updated pricing-model-v3.xlsx with the scenarios Karthik recommended.

Summary of proposed approach (for agreement):
- Meter: Azure private offer uses vCPU-month as the billed SKU. If Acme needs token-billing we include a static conversion appendix.
- Discounting: Bucketed approach (Option B):
    * Tier 1: 0–$150k/year -> list price (no auto discount)
    * Tier 2: $150k–$500k/year -> 10% off list
    * Tier 3: >$500k/year -> 20% off list
- Reseller passback: ResellerCorp gets 18% of net revenue for Tier 1, 16% for Tier 2, 12% for Tier 3. (Mark — you said 18/12; I proposed a graded band for expansion to keep economics aligned.)
- Minimum monthly floor: $5k/month for the passback to apply; below that, reseller commission is zero.

Example waterfall (short):
- List price: $1,000,000/year
- Tiered discount applied -> Net revenue: $820,000 (after 18% weighted discount example)
- Reseller passback (weighted per tier) -> $139,600 to ResellerCorp
- Redwood net recognized revenue -> $680,400 (numbers in workbook).

Next steps / asks:
1) Mark — confirm you can accept the 18/16/12 band or propose alternate bands.
2) Sara — confirm vCPU-month is acceptable for Acme or if you want tokens w/ conversion appendix.
3) Ben / Soojin / Karthik — can the finance & ops teams review the attached workbook and confirm whether the waterfall maps cleanly to our marketplace settlements format? Ben, can you run the sample scenario through marketplace billing?

If everyone is aligned, I’ll:
- create a private offer draft in the Azure marketplace UI with the SKU mapping,
- attach the reseller addendum for DocuSign (reseller-commission-term-sheet.pdf), and
- schedule a call for Wednesday to finalize.

Thanks all —
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
